Maud O’Connor Mysteries #3

What Happened That Night

Nicci French

4.03
7,566 ratings736 reviews
Rate this book
From international bestselling master of suspense Nicci French comes a hair-raising locked-room thriller about a group of old university friends with a killer in their midst.

Old friends, new secrets, one deadly reunion.

Tyler Green, accused of murdering his friend Leo on a graduation trip in 1993, has just been released from a commuted life sentence. In the three decades since his trial Tyler has been adamant that he’s innocent, and now he’s determined to confront whoever allowed him to take the fall while they walked free.

On a warm June evening in London, Tyler summons eight of his university friends to reunite for the first time since that fateful night. With wine—and accusations— flowing liberally, the reunion descends into violent chaos, and one friend will end the night with their throat slit in the upstairs bedroom…the same way that Leo’s was in 1993.

When Detective Inspector Maud O’Connor gets called to investigate, she has her own doubts about Tyler’s guilt, despite what his old friends, the rest of the Metropolitan Police Force, and even the Home Secretary would like her to believe….

Tyler Green Will Never Be Free is perfect for fans of Lucy Foley and other pulse-pounding locked-room mysteries in the Agatha Christie tradition.

About the author

Nicci French

82 books3,882 followers
Note: (Nicci Gerrard and Sean French also write separately.)

Nicci Gerrard was born in June 1958 in Worcestershire. After graduating with a first class honours degree in English Literature from Oxford University, she began her first job, working with emotionally disturbed children in Sheffield. In that same year she married journalist Colin Hughes.

In the early eighties she taught English Literature in Sheffield, London and Los Angeles, but moved into publishing in 1985 with the launch of Women's Review, a magazine for women on art, literature and female issues.

In 1987 Nicci had a son, Edgar, followed by a daughter, Anna, in 1988, but a year later her marriage to Colin Hughes broke down.

In 1989 she became acting literary editor at the New Statesman, before moving to the Observer, where she was deputy literary editor for five years, and then a feature writer and executive editor.

It was while she was at the New Statesman that she met Sean French.

Sean French was born in May 1959 in Bristol, to a British father and Swedish mother. He too studied English Literature at Oxford University at the same time as Nicci, also graduating with a first class degree, but their paths didn't cross until 1990. In 1981 he won Vogue magazine's Writing Talent Contest, and from 1981 to 1986 he was their theatre critic. During that time he also worked at the Sunday Times as deputy literary editor and television critic, and was the film critic for Marie Claire and deputy editor of New Society.

Sean and Nicci were married in Hackney in October 1990. Their daughters, Hadley and Molly, were born in 1991 and 1993.

By the mid-nineties Sean had had two novels published, The Imaginary Monkey and The Dreamer of Dreams, as well as numerous non-fiction books, including biographies of Jane Fonda and Brigitte Bardot.

In 1995 Nicci and Sean began work on their first joint novel and adopted the pseudonym of Nicci French. The Memory Game was published to great acclaim in 1997 followed by The Safe House (1998), Killing Me Softly (1999), Beneath the Skin (2000), The Red Room (2001), Land of the Living (2002), Secret Smile (2003), Catch Me When I Fall (2005), Losing You (2006) and Until It's Over (2008). Their latest novel together is What To Do When Someone Dies (2009).

Nicci and Sean also continue to write separately. Nicci still works as a journalist for the Observer, covering high-profile trials including those of Fred and Rose West, and Ian Huntley and Maxine Carr. Novels include Things We Knew Were True (2003), Solace (2005) and The Moment You Were Gone (2007). Sean's last novel is Start From Here (2004).

Nilufer Ozmekik
3,290 reviews64.9k followers
August 7, 2025
I think the Maud O’Connor series by this perfect thriller duo just keeps getting better—and this one shook me to the core. It even made me furious at the unfairness one of the characters had to endure (I won’t spoil it, but judging from the book’s title and opening, you’ll probably guess who I mean). By the end, I cried—and I’m not saying whether it was from heartbreak, relief, or both.

The mystery is tense and deeply layered, revolving around a group of old university friends whose past never truly stayed buried.At the center is Tyler Green, a man who has spent nearly thirty years in prison for a crime he insists he didn’t commit: the murder of his friend Leo at a student party in 1993. After his release, Tyler attends the dinner party where the eight remaining friends from that night reunite, reigniting the embers of secrets long buried. But history has a terrifying way of repeating itself. Another murder. The same method. The same room. And Tyler, once again, stands accused.

Enter DI Maud O’Connor—sharp, intuitive, and not easily swayed by public opinion. While the media, the public, and even the highest levels of government rush to convict Tyler all over again, Maud quietly begins to pull at the threads of the case. What she finds is a group of friends bonded by trauma, guilt, and self-preservation—and someone among them who is willing to kill to keep the past in the shadows.

This book tore me apart in the best way. The tension is palpable, the pacing razor-sharp, and the emotional undercurrent is devastating. I found myself enraged by the injustices, gripped by the slow-burn unraveling of each character, and ultimately heartbroken by what Tyler endured. (No spoilers—but the ending made me cry. Whether from sorrow or relief… I’ll let you decide.)

Nicci French doesn’t just write crime novels—they write human stories buried inside mystery. And this one? This is a career highlight. It’s the kind of book that lingers, one that makes you question how many lives are quietly ruined by convenient assumptions and rushed conclusions.

Absolutely my favorite in the Maud O’Connor series—ten out of ten stars! A must-read for fans of Lucy Foley, Agatha Christie, and anyone who loves a good psychological gut-punch wrapped in a mystery.

A very huge thanks to NetGalley and William Morrow for sharing this addictive, emotionally-charged final installment of the series as an advance reader copy in exchange for my honest thoughts—I’m truly grateful.

This is book three of three in the Maud O’Connor Mysteries. In this instalment, we meet a man about to be released from 29 years in prison.

Tyler Green was convicted of murdering Leo Bower and sentenced to 29 years. On his release, he insists he had something to do….

Years earlier, Tyler was a medical student on his way to becoming a doctor. He had a close-knit group of university friends who enjoyed each other’s company until one of them was found dead.

Tyler’s idea was to collaborate with Beatrice MacMillan and a university friend. She volunteered to host the reunion of his university friends. Interestingly, despite all that time, only one member had visited him in prison while everyone else was absent.

History seemed to be about to repeat itself in a cruel twist. The murder of another group member naturally led to suspicion falling on Tyler, given his conviction years earlier. His unwavering cries for innocence went unheard despite his pleas.

Enter Di Maud O’Connor. Much of the book unfolds before her arrival, reminiscent of a TV show where drama builds up before the police intervene. This is my favourite book in the series so far.

As a woman in a predominantly male force, Maud faces challenges but remains determined to pursue justice despite pressure to deliver results. Everyone thinks it’s an open and shut case so Maud gets to work.

Ultimately, we discover that the same murderer strikes again, but it’s not the person everyone suspects. Maud leaves no stone unturned…

October 30, 2025
"Tyler Green Will Never Be Free" by Nicci French is a cleverly constructed psychological thriller and the third in the Maud O’Connor Mysteries. I didn’t realize it was the third in the series, nor had I read the previous books, but that didn’t impact my enjoyment. It stands well on its own, and I had no issues following along.

The book follows the reunion of a group of old university friends and its aftermath. When they were students, one of them—Leo—was murdered, and another—Tyler Green—was convicted of his murder. He always claimed he was innocent. Now, almost thirty years later, Tyler is out of jail and asks his friends to reconnect, which they reluctantly agree to.

The reunion starts off as planned, but wine and accusations soon dampen the atmosphere and tensions rise. When another member of the group is found dead in the same manner as the first murder, suspicion falls on Tyler. After all, he is a convicted murderer. Detective Maud O’Connor is called to investigate, but she isn’t convinced Tyler is guilty. As the investigation unfolds, long-buried secrets and old wounds resurface.

The novel is a concoction of intrigue, psychological character study, and drama. The authors seamlessly weave themes of fallible human nature, morality, relationships, friendship, caring, abuse, bullying, justice—or the lack thereof—crime, and its consequences.

The story is told in third person, alternating between characters, and divided into two parts. The first part introduces the friends, giving us their backstories and psychological profiles, while the second focuses on Maud and the investigation.

The pacing of the mystery is somewhat slow, although it didn’t dampen my enjoyment. You won’t find any breathtaking tension here—the plot moves steadily, with limited action, focusing instead on the characters and atmosphere, which isn’t a bad thing.

I enjoyed the mix of psychological insight and suspense. It’s well-plotted, and what truly shines is the portrayal of the characters—their mindsets and the way their feelings of anger, fear, sadness, camaraderie, and pain feel so palpable. The authors excel at revealing character through both physical description and acute psychological observation.

I didn’t guess the identity of the perpetrator, and the curveballs thrown me back. I liked that Maud didn’t bow to outside pressures and insisted on conducting the investigation her own way, without prejudice. The writing is sharp and compelling, though it could use a bit of tightening, as the repetitions of the interrogations and the inclusion of some minor characters slowed down the pace.

Nicci French is the pen name of the husband-and-wife writing team Nicci Gerrard and Sean French, and the writing is so seamless that I couldn’t distinguish who wrote which parts. This is an exciting psychological thriller that keeps you guessing until the very last page. I enjoyed the book and its psychological depth, but the slow pacing and some repetitive scenes kept me from giving it five stars. I’m now eager to read the other two books in the series.

"Old friends, new secrets, one deadly reunion." Just what the doctor ordered.

* Thank you NetGalley and (publisher) for the opportunity to read this arc. All opinions are my own.
* Review on my blog: https://galibookish.blogspot.com/2025...

What Happened That Night is the third book in the Maud O’Connor series by best-selling British writing duo, Nicci French. After almost twenty-nine years in prison for the murder of his friend, Leo Bauer, fifty-one-year-old Tyler Green is released on licence. There’s just one thing he wants to do. Will Garvey is the only one of those present at that fateful midsummer weekend when Leo Bauer died, who actually visited him in prison. Tyler convinces him to arrange it, and Will talks Beatrice Macmillan, KC and wife of a cabinet minister, into hosting it.

On a midsummer Friday evening, eight (once) friends who have mostly not seen one another for three decades, and one much younger hanger-on, gather for dinner with Tyler Green. At the mention of atonement, he quickly disabuses them of the notion that he’s asking to be forgiven. Because he did not kill Leo Bauer.

One of the company is openly angry, observing of Tyler “Sitting there in judgement. Though how a convicted murderer can sit in judgement, I do not know.” It’s such an awful evening, most are wondering why they ever agreed to come. Before the night is out, one of their number is dead, and Tyler Green is, once again, in a prison cell.

DI Maud O’Connor, on call, is sent to the MP’s house by her boss with instructions not to make some kind of point: “Everyone’s going to be watching this one: the government, the press.” Maud insists DS Carrie Kessler assist her.

At the scene, it’s clear that the first attending officer has already concluded Tyler Green is the murderer. Carrie comments to Maud “Now I want it not to be Tyler Green, just to wipe the smile off his face.” Maud O’Connor definitely isn’t convinced of his guilt: “…if you were going to revenge yourself on someone, would you do it at a party that you yourself had asked for, in an enclosed space where it would be hard not to be seen, where you’d gathered all the witnesses of the first murder, and where you would be the immediate suspect?”

After interviewing Tyler, Carrie remarks “Either he’s a hardened criminal, or he’s the unluckiest man I’ve ever met, and that’s saying something.” To Tyler, she later summarises, “so basically, you came to this reunion, found out everyone’s weak spot, and exploited it until each person was in a state of anger and pain.” Hardly surprising someone was murdered?

As well as fending off the demands of her boss, putting up with incompetent colleagues and uncooperative prison officers, and trying to get the truth out of witnesses, Maud has spouses at her: “’I can make life very difficult for you.’ Maud grinned. ‘Join the queue,’ she said cheerfully.” She doesn’t always get her way, but she sure can hold her own, solving the case within thirteen hours, in time for lunch with an interesting man. Leave yourself some time once you start: the pages fly by but you won’t be able to put this one down. More of Maud O’Connor please! Brilliant British crime fiction.

Tyler Green was tot levenslang veroordeeld voor de moord op zijn studiegenoot Leo. Nu, dertig jaar later, is hij vrij. Voordat hij de draad van zijn leven weer kan oppakken wil hij een wens laten uitkomen: dat de vriendengroep van destijds een avond samen doorbrengt. Toen is de hele vriendengroep uit elkaar gevallen, maar Tyler wil dat ze samenkomen - waarvoor precies, dat weet niemand.

Oud-studiegenoot Beatrice, inmiddels getrouwd met een politicus, stelt haar huis beschikbaar. Al snel wordt duidelijk dat Tyler bijbedoelingen had toen hij deze reünie organiseerde. En dan valt er nog een dode… Tyler wordt nogmaals in hechtenis genomen, maar hij houdt vol dat hij onschuldig is. Vertelt hij de waarheid? 

Dit verhaal is opgedeeld in twee delen en het eerste deel begint met de vrijlating van Tyler Green. Hij heeft dertig jaar gevangen gezeten voor de dood op een studiegenoot en nu is hij weer vrij.

Hij wil vrijwel meteen een avond met zijn oude vriendengroep doorbrengen. Dus je leest ook snel vanuit verschillende personages. Eén hiervan is Beatrice, zij stelt haar huis beschikbaar.

Soms maak je sprongen naar het verleden en lees je meer over de vriendengroep. Het is nog onduidelijk wat er dertig jaar geleden op die bewuste dag is gebeurd, maar langzaamaan worden er steeds meer dingen uitgelegd.

De afwisseling van personages vond ik prettig, want zo kreeg je een beter beeld van de oude vriendengroep. Ook de sfeer tijdens het etentje werd goed op papier gezet, want het wordt duidelijk dat Tyler dit niet zonder reden wilde.

Vervolgens ga je naar het tweede gedeelte en lees je over Maud. Er blijkt een dode te zijn gevallen in het huis van Beatrice, dus er moet iets gruwelijk mis zijn gegaan tussen de oude vrienden, maar wat? En is Tyler weer de dader? Hij wordt sowieso weer opgepakt, maar Tyler beweert onschuldig te zijn. Lukt het Maud om achter de waarheid te komen?

Dit verhaal vond ik boeiend om te lezen. De dynamiek tussen de vriendengroep wordt goed beschreven en iedereen kon de dader zijn. Ik vond dat dit erg goed geheim bleef.

Het wordt niet heel spannend, maar ik vond het wel een heerlijk psychologisch verhaal.

Tyler Green, has been in prison for 29 years for murdering his friend Leo Bauer on a graduation trip in 1993. He is then released on licence and the first thing he wants to do is get his old university friends back together so he can close off this chapter of his life. Tyler has always maintained his innocence throughout his sentence, so if he were to find out who the real murderer was, that would be an added bonus.

The reunion is held at Beatrice Macmillan’s house, she is a KC and one of the more successful of the group of friends. The remainder are Ali, Will, Rudi, Marco, Clara, Jay and Ellen. The majority of the friends haven’t seen each other since that fateful night, and with the exception of Will none of the others went to visit Tyler in prison. Not even Tyler’s then girlfriend, Ali, who is now married to Will. With the alcohol flowing freely, the friends become loose lipped, and with it the secrets and accusations fly. Tragedy occurs when one of the friends is found murdered late into the party in an upstairs bedroom and in an eerily similar way to Leo’s death so many years earlier.

Detective Inspector Maud O’Connor is called in to investigate, but she not only ends up investigating this new murder, but is also drawn into the details of the historic murder.

This is the third in the DI Maud O’Connor series and as per the first two books, Maud comes into the story part way through. This allows the reader to focus on the story and the characters in the build up and really sets the scene well.

The majority of the characters are unlikeable, but this actually works well for this story, they all have complex lives now, and as secrets are revealed we find out how intertwined the friends were in each other’s lives back then. There are multiple layers to peel back, which keeps the story fresh and engaging.

I was honestly surprised when I found out who the culprit(s) was/were. There are plenty of people with a motive, so it really keeps you guessing and the way the story works itself out is plotted really well.

I’m a huge fan of Nicci French’s books, and this new Maud O’Connor series shows just why they are an auto-buy for me. Fast paced, gripping and engrossing. I really enjoyed it.

Another tour-de-force from the Suffolk-based crime writing couple with its highly likeable protagonist.

A slow-burning, deeply compelling mystery that hinges on tension and atmosphere.

After spending 30 years in prison for the murder of his university friend Leo, Tyler Green is released, still maintaining his innocence. He arranges a gathering of the 8 friends who were present on that tragic night for a reunion in London, seeking answers about what truly happened. When another murder occurs late in the evening after dinner, Detective Inspector Maud O'Connor steps in to investigate. Tyler is immediately re-arrested and returned to prison but Maud isn't sure. As old secrets unravel and with the past repeating itself, Maud and DS Carrie Kessler must determine whether Tyler is a psychopathic killer seeking revenge or a scapegoat set up once again.

This is one of those locked room type mysteries where the killer is hidden in plain sight and I suspected each person in turn. What makes the set up work so well in this case is the quiet paranoia and heavy sense of long-buried guilt among the friends. The story shifts focus from simple procedural tracking to a nuanced exploration of shifting loyalties, unreliable memories, past hurts as well as embarrassments, and evidence of how 30 years of secrets can corrode relationships. The characters were so well-developed and sharply drawn and as the friends reveal their stories in police interviews, Maud is laser focused on the timeline and their explanations about the night. The tension builds and the suspense escalates as things soon crystalize while Maud hones in on the likely killer and obtains the confessions. I could barely put this down wondering who did it making all sorts of guesses. It was a very engrossing book. I've read the first in this series but missed the second and now will definitely go back to catch up.

I was able to listen to the audio book while also following along in the e-book ARC, both provided by the publishers. The narrator, Sophie Roberts, did a very good job of voicing all the characters, giving them unique and distinguishing tones. She had the appropriate dramatic flair which enhanced my immersion into the book and increased my appreciation of the story.

Note - this book was previously titled Tyler Green Will Never Be Free

The book is centred around Tyler green who has just served almost a 30 year sentence for killing his best friend Leo Bauer. He summons his group of friends who were there on the night Leo died as a reunion. This goes sideways when one of his friends are found dead on the same night, with all evidence pointing to Tyler putting his new found freedom in jeopardy. It’s up to detective Maud O’Connor to investigate and find the truth behind the murder.

Overall it’s not a bad book, will keep this as a series I can invest in. I am interested in the direction of the book and the plot. I would also like to read more about Maud’s character as enough though there are glimpses, there still isn’t a lot of her individual personality.

Nicci French is toch wel een gevestigde waarde in thrillerland en ook met hun nieuwste boek wordt dit weer eens bevestigd.

Het boek start met voor elk personage een apart hoofdstuk. Dit was dan wel even in het verhaal komen want het zijn nog wel best veel personages. Eenmaal ze elkaar ontmoeten switchte het perspectief tijdens het hoofdstuk af en toe en daar ben ik eerlijk gezegd geen fan van. Maar het wende gelukkig snel want vanaf dat punt zat ik helemaal in het verhaal.

Het verhaal bestaat uit twee delen. In deel één heeft Tyler Green na zijn vrijlating een reünie gepland met zijn oude vrienden. Tyler heeft net bijna dertig jaar vastgezeten voor de moord op Leo, een lid van de vriendengroep. Hoewel ze allemaal hun bedenkingen hebben, is iedereen komen opdagen. Ze komen samen in het huis van Beatrice die nu als jurist werkt en gehuwd is met een minister. De avond loopt uit de hand als Tyler verklaart dat hij Leo niet heeft vermoord maar dat dit dus iemand van de anderen geweest moet zijn.

In het tweede deel wordt Maud O’Connor opgeroepen voor een moord in het huis van de minister. Tyler Green is meteen de hoofdverdachte maar Maud wil het onderzoek grondig doen en gaat ook de anderen verhoren. Ondanks dat alle pijlen richting Tyler wijzen, wil zij hem nog niet meteen beschuldigen en gaat ze - tegen de zin van haar oversten - ook de andere aanwezigen verhoren.

De schrijfstijl van Nicci French is meeslepend en diept de personages voldoende uit. Ondanks de vele hoofdpersonages is het vrij snel duidelijk wie wie is en hoe de onderlinge relaties in elkaar zitten. De emoties van Tyler komen soms wel binnen. Als hij weer de gevangenis in vliegt nadat hij pas is vrijgelaten. Vreselijk. Dan is er zelfs nog maar de vraag of hij effectief schuldig was én is. Het is niet nagelbijtend spannend, maar er is eerder sprake van een psychologische spanning die je aandacht vasthoudt tot op het eind. Op het einde valt alles mooi in elkaar.

Ondanks dat dit het derde deel in de serie rond Maud O’Connor is, is dit boek zeker losstaand te lezen.

Dertig jaar lang zat Tyler Green vast voor moord. Nu is hij vrij. Voor één avond brengt hij zijn oude vrienden weer samen, rond een zorgvuldig gedekte tafel.
Wat begint als een ogenschijnlijk onschuldig etentje, krijgt al snel een ongemakkelijke ondertoon. Oude loyaliteiten blijken broos, herinneringen onbetrouwbaar en zwijgen gevaarlijker dan spreken. Wanneer de avond ontaardt en er iets afschuwelijks gebeurt, wijst alles opnieuw in één richting: Tyler.
Maar rechercheur Maud O’Connor twijfelt. Is Tyler werkelijk een man die nooit is veranderd, of juist iemand die te goed weet wat hij doet?

Mijn ervaring:
Heerlijk! Opnieuw weet Nicci French me te verrassen met dit nieuwe deel. De verhaallijn is origineel, sterk en indrukwekkend, en bovendien scherp en zorgvuldig uitgewerkt. Het verhaal is niet alleen spannend, maar ook diep menselijk en psychologisch doordacht. Vanaf de eerste pagina hangt er een beklemmende, bijna unheimische sfeer, die gedurende het verhaal steeds verder wordt opgebouwd. De schrijfstijl is levendig, vlot en krachtig, waardoor je moeiteloos door het boek heen leest.

De personages vormen zonder twijfel het hart van dit verhaal. Hoofdpersonage Tyler roept direct sympathie en compassie op: een man die na bijna dertig jaar gevangenisstraf terugkeert in een wereld die hij nauwelijks nog herkent, worstelend met zijn verleden en met de mensen die ooit zijn vrienden waren. Die oude vrienden zijn stuk voor stuk complex, intrigerend en onvolmaakt, vol tegenstrijdigheden. Hun motieven, geheimen en gezamenlijke geschiedenis maken hun gedrag begrijpelijk, of juist extra verdacht.

De verhaallijn is slim en met precisie opgebouwd. Het verhaal begint met Tylers vrijlating en een ogenschijnlijk onschuldige reünie-avond, maar al snel sluipen emotie en spanning stap voor stap het verhaal binnen. Nicci French verrast met krachtige wendingen, verborgen motieven en geheimen die langzaam aan het licht komen. Als lezer blijf je voortdurend twijfelen: wie is te vertrouwen en wat is de echte waarheid? Thema’s als schuld, vriendschap en gerechtigheid zijn knap verweven in het verhaal. En dan is er natuurlijk rechercheur Maud O’Connor, wiens rol gaandeweg groeit. Haar innerlijke strijd en scherpe analyse geven het verhaal extra diepgang en emotionele lading.

Tyler komt nooit meer vrij is een pakkend, verrassend en indrukwekkend derde deel van de Maud O’Connor-serie. Het psychologische web van motieven, leugens en geheimen, gecombineerd met de sterke wendingen en gebeurtenissen, zorgt ervoor dat dit verhaal je van begin tot eind in zijn greep houdt.

What Happened That Night is a tense crime thriller, related from multiple narrative perspectives and, with the exception of a short prologue and several flash-back sequences, taking place over a single scorching Midsummer's weekend in London.

51-year-old Tyler Green has just emerged from a 29-year prison sentence, having been convicted as a university undergraduate for the brutal murder of a member of his friendship group, Leo Bauer. Having remained in touch with only one of his university friends, Will, Tyler makes a strange request - that all the surviving members of that fateful weekend trip gather together.

Hosting the dinner is barrister Beatrice Macmillan, who holds grave misgivings about inviting these people with whom she was once close into her plush London home. Other attendees are Will and his wife Ali, who had been Tyler's girlfriend at the time of Leo's death, writer Rudi, who'd had a clandestine relationship with Beatrice during their undergraduate days, struggling musician Marco and his much-younger partner Kristin, ebullient earth-mother Ellen, matter-of-fact Clara and her ex-boyfriend Jay, who has suffered from debilitating mental illness through most of his life.

Despite their discomfort at facing the man who many of them believe killed their friend and cast a shadow over their transition into adult life, all those present on the night of Leo Bauer's death are once again under the same roof. Sparks fly, accusations and recriminations are hurled across Beatrice's carefully prepared grazing table and blows are exchanged in her idyllic garden. Tyler makes the startling announcement that he did not actually kill Leo, but that he knows that one of those present did!

As midnight strikes on Midsummer's night, a scream echoes from the upstairs floor of Beatrice's lavish home - one of their number lies dead in a manner not dissimilar to the murder of Leo 29 years previously.

At this point in the narrative, MET D.I. Maud O'Connor and her loyal colleague D.S. Cassie Kessler, swing into action to interview the witness-suspects and determine who is responsible for this present-day crime. Despite considerable pressure from the hierarchy to clear the matter up quickly and discretely (Beatrice's husband is a cabinet Minister), preferably by confirming the easy assumption that Tyler Green has killed again, O'Connor refuses to be diverted from a comprehensive and objective investigation.

I thoroughly enjoyed the police procedural / mystery narrative of What Happened That Night and intend to read the previous two books in Nicci French's Maud O'Connor series. However, the part of the story that resonated most with me was the cathartic effect that the reunion with their university cohort has on the cast of suspects. Perhaps I particularly felt this because these fictional characters were around the same age as myself and I found many parallels between my own recollections and experiences and those of several of the characters (none of my university friends was murdered though, it should be said!). The fact that Tyler's life has effectively been suspended for three decades causes each of Beatrice's guests to consider how their own lives have changed over that time. None of the group are completely satisfied with their lives in the present, for a variety of reasons, and it's confronting to be face-to-face with those who knew you when your potential and passion were at their greatest. Marco's younger girlfriend, Kristin - who has never met any of these people before - works as a foil, somewhat brashly holding up a mirror to the self-delusion, face-saving and hidden resentments that simmer just below the surface.

What Happened That Night is a stimulating read, which I'd enthusiastically recommend to any reader who enjoys tautly-plotted, character-driven crime thrillers.

This book is so engaging! It's the third in the Maud O'Connor series, but also works perfectly as a standalone. In Part 1 of the book, we meet a group of old college friends who get together after many years when one member of the friend group, Tyler Green, is released from prison on parole. Tyler was convicted of killing another one of their friends which understandably caused the others to become estranged from Tyler, but also fragmented the whole group. After serving almost thirty years in prison, Tyler still insists he's innocent, but why does he want to get together with the people who were so quick to abandon him?

Maud, as well as DS Carrie Kessler come into the picture in Part 2, The reunion goes wrong and Maud is called in to investigate yet another death occurring with the same group of people as decades earlier. Secrets from the past and the present come into play in this difficult case, but I had confidence that Maud would figure it out. My theory as to the killer was completely wrong, and it was fun to be surprised. I loved this book and recommend it to both fans of French and readers who haven't tried her books yet.

I received an advance copy of this ebook from William Morrow books, but my review is voluntary and unbiased.

Een Nicci French: dat was lang geleden! Dit soort boeken koos ik vroeger in de bibliotheek met mijn moeder uit. Toen al was ik er gek op en nog steeds houd ik van thrillers. Maar wel op zijn tijd, want ik houd van afwisseling in mijn boeken. Die tijd was er nu en ik heb dit boek in een zucht uitgelezen.

Tyler Green komt na bijna 30 jaar vast te hebben gezeten vrij en organiseert een etentje met zijn oude vriendengroep. Deze vrienden weten allemaal waarvoor Tyler vast heeft gezeten - sterker nog: ze waren bij het delict. Tijdens de reünie komt veel oud zeer boven. Men wil bovendien weten wat de reden achter de reünie is. Dan valt er nog een dode en dat zet alles op zijn kop. Was het 30 jaar geleden wel zo gegaan als iedereen dacht?

Ik vlóóg door dit boek heen door de vlotte schrijfstijl. Het heeft korte hoofdstukjes en leest heel gemakkelijk weg. De perspectieven wisselen heel gauw - wat het aanvankelijk een beetje ingewikkeld maakt vanwege de vele karakters die je moet leren kennen - en daardoor blijf je als lezer geboeid. Ik heb me geen seconde verveeld in het eerste deel, terwijl ik in meerdere reviews juist lees dat men het eerste deel van het boek over het etentje zelf soms wat saai vind. Ik vond juist ergens in het tweede deel tijdens het politieonderzoek dat er op een gegeven moment weinig schot in de zaak was en dat er naar mijn smaak iets te veel herhaling was door de verhoren die plaatsvonden. De inspecteur die de zaak onderzoekt, Maud O'Connor, stelt dan namelijk allerlei vragen aan de getuigen die je als lezer nog niet helemaal kunt plaatsen. Dat is op zich prima, maar de opbouw naar de ontknoping duurde mij wel net iets te lang.

Ik moest mezelf er wel telkens aan herinneren dat ik over personages van in de 50 las en niet over jonge mensen in de leeftijd van 20 tot 30. Ik ben wel benieuwd of andere lezers dat gevoel ook hadden. De personages gedroegen zich naar mijn mening vrij jong. Ergens vind ik dat ook heel tof gedaan door de auteurs, aangezien dit aangeeft dat de betrokkenen terug in de tijd gaan en ik hun oude rollen vervallen als zij hun jeugdvrienden weer zien. Maar anderzijds kon ik de karakters in mijn hoofd niet zien als mensen van middelbare leeftijd en dat vond ik wel een beetje jammer.

Wat ik van de ontknoping vind? Ik werkte er heel erg naartoe in mijn hoofd tijdens het lezen, maar vond hem uiteindelijk niet erg spectaculair. Ook zeker niet slecht hoor, maar ik bleef niet verbijsterd van de kunde van de auteurs achter. Het was niet alsof ik dit zelf door middel van deductie had kunnen bedenken en dan voelt het toch willekeuriger, omdat je als lezer informatie mist. Desalniettemin een heel vermakelijke thriller met een pakkende setting. Perfect voor mee op vakantie, echt een hoofd uit-boek. Ook een leuk boek om met anderen over te kletsen, dus ik ga oma appen.

Прочетох повечето книги на Ники Френч през годините, но мисля, че романите им стават все по-добри. Те са по-сложни, емоционални и многопластови, което тази поредица ясно демонстрира, точно за това ми е любимата им поредица, като всяка книга става с пъти по-добра. 🥰



Тази трета книга от поредицата за Мод О'Конър е разделена на две половини. Първата е за събиране на приятели от университетските им години, събрани след 29 години от Тайлър Грийн, мъж, осъден за убийството на един от членовете на тяхната група. Докато опознаваме всеки герой, бързо става ясно, че въпреки че Тайлър е прекарал близо три десетилетия зад решетките, останалите също не са съвсем свободни. Но пък – кой е той, че да съди? Сега с напредването на нощта ние биваме въвлечени в живота и историята им, преплитайки сложни нишки и разкриване на мрачни тайни. Във втората половина на книгата Мод О'Конър се намесва с разплитането на станало убийство от въпросната вечер.



Разказано от множество гледни точки, това е интригуващо изследване на характера. Наистина хитра мистерия за убийство, където дълго пазени тайни излизат наяве с шокиращи последици, засягащи всеки един замесен човек. Ескалиращата мъка, загубените животи, разделенията, бъркотията и чувството за заплаха са напълно осезаеми. Има върхове и спадове, които стават все по-високи и по-дълбоки с напредването на катастрофалната вечер.



Това което е интересно и оригинално в поредицата за инспектор Мод О'Конър е, че, винаги остава леко на заден план. Научаваме достатъчно за нея, за да разберем какъв детектив е, но личният ѝ живот никога не засенчва разследването. Защото при повечето автори е точно обратното.
